newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH ELECTRONICS INDUSTRY SEES STABLE 1997 ROI.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH ELECTRONICS INDUSTRY SEES STABLE 1997 ROI.

text.p: The Finnish electric and electronics industry on Monday said it expected 1997 earnings performance in terms of return on investment to stay at around 20 percent.

For the past three years, the industry has charted returns on invested capital of over 20 percent, ombudsman Markku Alhonen of the Federation of Finnish Electrical and Electronics Industries told Reuters on the sidelines of a news conference.
"The trend has been clear. Return on investment will stay at about 20 percent," Alhonen said, referring to 1997.
"Net sales have grown so fast that I don't think the percentage (return on investment) figure can get much better -- at least, not in the near future," Alhonen said.
The federation said it expected production growth of over 10 percent in 1997 and 1998, with the value of output expected to rise to 65 billion markka in 1998 from a good 50 billion in 1996.

Output by the telecommunications industry in 1996 rose to half of the value of the entire electric and electronics sector, federation chairman Matti Alahuhta, also president of Nokia Oy's Telecommuniations business group, told the news conference.
"Telecommunications is also predicted to continue growing the fastest during the next five years," Alahuhta said.
